SE3110: Quality Management in Software Engineering
LegalEase AI: Enterprise Omnichannel Legal Practice Management and Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Subsystem

This report records tool-based testing and quality evaluation of the LegalEase AI system developed for SE3090. It preserves the SE3110 test plan, case designs, defects and contribution disclosures while distinguishing actual execution evidence from historical claims and unresolved requirements.

Publication revision: 8 October 2026 (Asia/Colombo). Approved tested source 05359214df52, including fixes f360e4ac21f1, is published on Wishwa2002/Intelligent-legal-service, branch se3110-qmse-testing. Original development history is preserved; no deployment or submission occurred. GitHub CI did not trigger for this branch. Available SE3090 Version 3.0 reference reviewed; formal approval unconfirmed. Original, 51-page and pre-publication 60-page reports are preserved.

Repository provenance: Wishwa2002/Intelligent-legal-service is the original group development repository. Its main/develop/feature histories retain recorded authors and dates; the new testing branch preserves that ancestry. Testing effort was prioritised by risk. The table links each risk to the requirement it threatens and the test area that addresses it.
Verify that the key features of all four business components behave as specified (FR-01 to FR-16).
Demonstrate at least one complete integrated workflow across Flutter, the .NET API, PostgreSQL, the Python AI mesh and the React clerk portal.
Measure performance against NFR-01 (API p95 < 200 ms, AI < 1.5 s) and verify security controls (JWT, RBAC, BCrypt, prompt-injection defence).
Record actual results, mark every test Passed or Failed, log defects, fix important ones and retest.

Keep reusable automated test scripts in the published testing branch and retain native reports, screenshots and final documents in the separately supplied evidence package so results can be reproduced and explained.

Additional non-functional types were selected where relevant: reliability/recovery (R7, AI outage must not break booking) and usability/compatibility (responsive web and mobile parity, NFR-06). Accessibility checks with Lighthouse/axe are listed as a recommended extension.

Flutter SDK recovery enabled a genuine web build and actual browser workflow, including upload and synchronized completion. The 49 existing Flutter unit/widget cases also pass.
